label: Formulated the Pragmatic Maxim in How to Make Our Ideas Clear
description: Charles Sanders Peirce formulated and introduced the concept of "The Pragmatic Maxim", which became a seminal contribution in epistemology philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in epistemology.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 19th Century Divergences as part of Charles Sanders Peirce's canonical writings.

label: Founded Pragmatism, which James popularized and personalized
description: William James was fundamentally influenced by Charles Sanders Peirce's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Charles Sanders Peirce's perspective to William James's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the 19th Century Divergences era.

label: Anticipated scientific fallibilism and evolutionary epistemology
description: Karl Popper was fundamentally influenced by Charles Sanders Peirce's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Charles Sanders Peirce's perspective to Karl Popper's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 19th Century Divergences across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.
